ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0), Swiss Federal Act on the Supervision of Financial Markets (FINMA Act, SR 956.1), Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) Arts. 627 and 697j, Swiss Commercial Register Ordinance (SR 221.411), Swiss Federal Ordinance on the Central Business Name Index, and the Swiss Federal Council's Swiss Sanctions Regulations under SR 946.231. UBO obligations also arise under FINMA Circular 2020/01 and the Federal Act on the International Automatic Exchange of Information (AEOI Act, SR 653.1).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport or national ID copy of each UBO and signatory shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport office or registrar of civil status in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified certificate of incorporation and register extract of any corporate UBO
Bank reference letter and source of funds statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Swiss consular legalization where bank apostille unavailable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, directors, authorized signatories and commercial counterparties against the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) sanctions lists, Swiss Federal Office for Customs and Border Safety and SECO embargo provisions, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated sanctions, and domestic Swiss PEP and adverse-media databases. Screening must be performed prior to notarization and continuously during the business relationship. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for politically exposed persons, source-of-wealth opacity, links to high-risk jurisdictions, or the presence of crypto-asset payment rails. The registered office and bank opening process require production of an AMLA-compliant beneficial owner disclosure, and any discrepancy triggers a report to the Swiss Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Swiss Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex / L'Index central des raison de société / Indice centrale dei nomi delle ditte) operated by the Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property and coordinated with the cantonal Commercial Register Offices through the Swiss Commercial Register platform (Registre du commerce / Handelsregister / Registro di commercio).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A legal entity name may be entered in any of the official Swiss languages (German, French, Italian) and, under certain conditions, in English. When using transliteration, national law requires the name to render correctly in the Latin script and must avoid phonetic conflict with existing protected names. The name must not be misleading, untruthful, or cause confusion with the existing registered trademarks. Legal-form suffixes must abide by the Civil Code and Commercial Register rules: an Aktiengesellschaft may use the suffix 'Aktiengesellschaft' or 'AG' in German, 'Société Anonyme' or 'SA' in French, or 'Società Anonima' or 'SA' in Italian; a mixed-language form may require a prevailing company-language declaration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banque, Bankgeschäft, Sparkasse, Vorsorge, Fond, Fondsleitung, Kotierte, Asset Management, Anlagefonds
Versicherung, assurance, assicurazione, insurance, Rückversicherung, Rückversicherung (insurance-related tokens)
Swiss, Suisse, Svizzera, Helvetia, Helvetic, or any other combination which implies a federal or sovereign connection
Confederation, Eidgenossenschaft, Bund, Confédération, Confederazione (requires state authorization)
Canton names, municipality names, and official coats of arms (other than the legal entity's actual registered seat with evidentiary requirement)
Kantonalbank or other regulated state-institution labels

Blockchain, Cryptovalue, Crypto, Decentralized, Stablecoin, Stiftung, Trust, Fiduciary, and any trust or endowment form indissociable from the AG (without special license from FINMA or the Cantonal Commercial Register)
Title such as 'Holding' unless asset management is actual and verifiable
Words that are objectively misleading as to the company purpose, especially implying an insurance or financial institution license without FINMA authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservation is valid for 30 days. An extension may be filed through the competent cantonal commercial registry before the expiry, supported by a renewed notarized application. In case of rejection, the notary or applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the Cantonal Commercial Registrar Supervisory Authority (Federal Commercial Register Office coordination) within 10 days of receipt of the negative decision; the appeal must contain alternative proposed name tokens. If the appeal remains unsuccessful, the applicant may pursue the complaint before the Cantonal Administrative Court or, in final resort, the Swiss Federal Supreme Court in Lausanne according to Art. 82 and 89 of the Federal Act on the Federal Supreme Court (SR 173.110). Re-application is permitted after a statutory cooling-off period if the conflict grounds are removed, but the file demand must be re-notarized and refiled through the notary.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office in the sense of a mere postal address, shared mailbox only or an unattended address without management presence is not acceptable to the Swiss Commercial Register. A physical registered office located within the canton is required, with actual administration capacity. However, a non-hospitality flexible workspace arrangement such as a business center with a contractual physical desk, administrative office, or mailbox and meeting room access may be accepted where the company can receive official correspondence and documents during opening hours. This industry (mobile utility app development) carries no statutory operational establishment that would condition the registered seat; the decisive factor is genuine administrative existence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection, quantified at approximately 15%-25% during the first two years after registration in the canton of Zug due to enhanced commercial substance scrutiny; inspections by the cantonal migration, tax and commercial-register authorities increase where the administrative office does not correspond to actual management activity. The likelihood of an unannounced visit is moderate (30%-40%) if the registered office is a virtual office provider with no evidence of continuous administrative operation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (OR/PCO), Articles 620–763; relevant capital provisions at Articles 632–637; board powers at Article 716a
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the Canton of Zug, under the Federal Department of Justice and Police
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association (Statuten), notarized and filed for entry in the Commercial Register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: For an Aktiengesellschaft, minimum share capital is CHF 100,000. At formation, each subscriber must pay in at least 20% of the nominal value per share, but in no case less than CHF 50,000 total; these funds must be deposited in a blocked Swiss bank account in the company's name and may be released only upon presentation of the final Commercial Register extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: The Company's incorporation deed and articles are ratified; subscriptions to 1,000 registered shares at CHF 100 par value, being the entire share capital of CHF 100,000, are confirmed and accepted; CHF 50,000 minimum paid-in capital is approved for transfer from the blocked capital escrow account to the company's operational account; the registered office at [Canton Zug address] is adopted; signature rules are set at two signatures for management; named officers as Chief Executive Officer and Vorsitzender (Chair) are appointed; and the board is authorized to complete commercial register formalities, obtain tax IDs and licenses, and open Swiss bank accounts. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Commercial Register Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of Canton Zug via Zefix online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed company name through the Zefix (Central Business Index) pre-clearance interface, ensuring no identical or misleading name and that the name reflects the business purpose of mobile utility software. State the ISIC 6201 activity and pay the applicable name inspection fee.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Business purpose description with ISIC/NAICS codes
Identification document of the applicant or director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to confusion or conflict, submit a revised application with three alternative names within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Deed of Incorporation and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Notary Public licensed in the Canton of Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and review the Deed of Incorporation and Articles (Statuten). The notary verifies the identity and capacity of the incorporators, share capital structure, registered office, and initial board members, then authenticates the signatures. All subscribers must execute the deed in person or by valid power of attorney.
required_dossiers: Notarized statutory deed
Articles of Association (Statuten)
Shareholder register with 1,000 registered shares at CHF 100 par value
Passports or identity cards of shareholders and directors
Declaration of Swiss residence for any resident director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a statutory defect, execute a supplementary notarial corrective deed within 10 days and re-file the document set.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Capital Deposit and Swiss Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank or private bank accepting Aktiengesellschaft clients in Canton Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked share capital account in the company's name and deposit the statutory minimum paid-in capital of CHF 50,000. The bank will issue a capital confirmation (Freigabebestätigung) that expressly restricts disposal until registration. After the Commercial Register entry is complete, the bank releases the funds to the company's operating account.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarized deed
Articles of Association
Identity and beneficial ownership declarations (CDB 16)
Bank account opening questionnaire and AML/KYC form
Statement of business purpose and payment rails, including Apple IAP and Google Play Billing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the source of funds or control structure, provide certified ownership documentation and source-of-wealth declarations; if the bank delays, substitute a registered Swiss bank and reopen within 3 additional days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Corporate Governance Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Aktiengesellschaft
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting on the basis of the notarized deed. Adopt the pro-forma board resolution, confirm share subscriptions, registered office, banking mandate, signature rules, and officer appointments. Approve delegated authority to complete the commercial register filing and to obtain all operational and tax licenses.
required_dossiers: Notice and agenda of the first board meeting
Pro-forma board resolution signed by all directors
Minutes of the first board meeting
Specimen signatures of directors and authorized signatories
Board mandate and capitalization table
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the board cannot obtain quorum, hold an extraordinary meeting by written circular resolution unanimously adopted by all directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Filing and Official Gazette Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of Canton Zug via Zefix/eGRIS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation application with the Commercial Register using the official electronic or paper forms. Attach the notarized deed, articles, board resolution, bank capital confirmation, and specimen signatures. Upon approval, the authority assigns the company identification number (UID) and publishes the formation notice in the Swiss Official Gazette (SOG).
required_dossiers: Official incorporation application form
Notarized Deed of Incorporation
Articles of Association
Bank blocked capital confirmation
First board meeting minutes and resolution
Specimen signature cards
Name reservation confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or request for clarification, respond within 30 days with corrected filings and sworn declarations; if the application lapses, file a new application and pay the registry fee again.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Social Insurance, and Operational Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA); Canton Zug Tax Administration; AHV/Ausgleichskasse; SUVA; Municipal Trade Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the UID and Commercial Register extract, register for VAT if annual taxable sales exceed CHF 100,000 or opt for voluntary low-risk VAT registration; register for corporate income tax and capital tax in Canton Zug; register employees and working directors for old-age, survivors', and disability insurance (AHV/IV/EO) and for accident insurance (UVG). If a physical office is opened, file the cantonal fire and structural occupancy clearance. No specific industrial manufacturing permit is required for the mobile utility app activity.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug)
UID confirmation letter
VAT registration form
Company passport with Swiss address
Foreign ownership and beneficial owner declarations
Employee registration forms for directors if salaried
Office occupancy or fire safety clearance if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File late registrations through voluntary self-disclosure, pay any required contribution or flat-rate penalty, and obtain a compliance confirmation letter to cure the omission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for software and mobile utility app activity; if any ancillary hardware distribution arises, contact the Canton Zug Department of Economic Affairs and the Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IPI) for trademark and import considerations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit required; the company requires only the Commercial Register entry, tax registrations, and, where applicable, standard Apple/License and Google Play Developer Console merchant agreements for app distribution.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category 0; pure software and digital service activity with no physical emission source, no factory, and no environmentally significant installation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; zero direct discharge of wastewater or air pollutants. Indirectly, the company must comply with Swiss rules on electronic records, data center energy efficiency, and, if disposing of IT hardware, the Ordinance on the Return, Taking Back and Disposal of Electrical and Electronic Equipment (ORDEE) and RoHS requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural load inspections are not required for the virtual software operation unless a physical office is rented in Canton Zug. If an office is occupied, the company must obtain a cantonal fire safety clearance, ensure workplace compliance under Swiss Labour Law (ArG), and complete the SUVA occupational accident insurance notification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC), Eigerstrasse 65, 3003 Bern. Official portals: www.estv.admin.ch (incl. VAT eServices, MWST/MWTR), www.uid.admin.ch (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer / UID registry), and www.ezv.admin.ch for customs/export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities with a Swiss VAT nexus (supply of goods stored in Switzerland, or B2C/B2B supply of services to Swiss recipients with turnover > CHF 100,000 p.a.) must first obtain a Swiss UID (business identification number) from the Federal Statistical Office via the UID portal, submitting the UID application form or the FTA's 'Registration of a foreign enterprise for VAT' form. The UID is assigned within 1-2 weeks and simultaneously serves as the VAT registration number (MWST-Nr) when the VAT registration declaration (Formular 754/Fiche 754) is filed. Non-established foreign companies without a Swiss branch may register online via FTA eService 'Registration for VAT purposes' and must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative (business agent with Swiss residency) if turnover exceeds CHF 100,000. A customs account at the Federal Office for Customs (e-dec web) is required for export declarations. Once registered, the VAT return must be filed electronically each quarter (or semi-annually/annual under simplified prior-authorization) and the UID must be printed on invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope_Reference: an Aktiengesellschaft (AG) is a resident corporation fully taxable on worldwide income; Swiss federal taxation applies a single flat rate (18.04% effective CIT incl. federal direct tax of ~8.5% after deduction), while cantonal/communal taxes apply income and capital taxes on a territorial/effective-nexus basis (profits attributable to a Swiss establishment or real property are taxable in Switzerland). No pass-through treatment is available for AG; shareholders are taxed only on distributed dividends (participation relief applies at 50-100% for qualifying holdings); CFC/hybrid rules follow OECD BEPS standards without mandatory check-the-box elections.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland has no US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections relevant to an AG: (i) VAT group taxation election under Art. 21 MWSTG/VAT Act for closely-linked enterprises (one VAT group, single tax number) — requires at least 70% voting/equity control and uniform management; (ii) voluntary VAT registration for small businesses below the CHF 100,000 threshold (Art. 34 VAT Act) allowing input VAT recovery; (iii) election for net-tax-rate (saldo method) for companies with turnover up to CHF 5,030,000 p.a. instead of exact input deduction; (iv) partial taxation/dividend relief: election to apply Swiss participation exemption (Art. 69 DBG) — not a check-the-box but an annual, binding declaration in the tax return; (v) no hybrid-mismatch election under Swiss ordinary law; Swiss tax treaties follow OECD BEPS Action 2 and the domestic rule disfavours hybrid structures via substance requirements and abuse clauses. Any election is made in writing to the cantonal tax administration, irrevocable for the fiscal year concerned.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée / Imposta sul valore aggiunto) — Swiss Federal VAT Act (MWSTG) of 12 June 2009
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 worldwide annual taxable turnover (consolidated, excluding exempt supplies) for Swiss-domiciled businesses (Art. 10 VAT Act). Since 1 Jan 2018, non-Swiss businesses providing electronic, telecom and digital services to Swiss private consumers (B2C) must register for VAT if their worldwide turnover exceeds CHF 100,000, and they must charge 8.1% VAT on Swiss B2C sales. Small businesses with turnover below CHF 100,000 may apply for exemption (Art. 11 VAT Act) but forfeit input VAT recovery. There is no separate state-level sales tax; the canton of Valais and others apply local tourist taxes outside VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a mandatory real-time fiscal-clearance or digital-stamping system. VAT returns are filed via FTA eServices (e-Steuererklärung MWST) with structured JSON/XML via the SWICO interface; no government pre-approval of invoices is required. Since 2023, the QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) is mandatory for any Swiss payment slip in CHF, embedding an electronic invoice payload; Peppol (UBL 2.1) e-invoicing is voluntarily supported by Swiss ERP providers and banks. B2B invoice retention obligations (10 years) apply, and the VAT invoice must contain: supplier UID/MWST number, recipient UID (for B2B), date, description, tax rate, and amount. Audit authorities may require digital export of underlying ledger data, but no transaction-level clearance API or e-verification token is imposed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of goods: 0% VAT under Art. 23(1)(a) VAT Act applies to movable goods physically transferred abroad (direct transport out of Switzerland by the supplier, the customer, or a commissioned carrier) provided that export is proven and the goods leave Switzerland within 30 days of the last invoice (or 60 days with extension). Export of services: 0% applies to services supplied to customers with a business seat or a residence abroad, including mobile application license downloads and subscriptions, if the recipient is a foreign VAT-liable enterprise or a private individual resident abroad and the service is not attributable to a Swiss permanent establishment; digital distribution via Apple IAP/Google Play requires proof that the end-customer is non-Swiss (store jurisdiction, billing address, platform seller reports). Certain services linked to Swiss real property or tangible goods remain taxable at 8.1% and do not qualify for zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (e-dec/Swiss-Impex exit confirmation or the A.I. G/E-form with customs stamp or NCTS exit movement reference number)
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / CMR consignment note or equivalent proof of physical dispatch/transport contract
Export invoice with supplier UID/MWST number, recipient address (foreign), goods/service description, and explicit 0% rate indication

Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 payment proof from a Swiss or foreign bank confirming the foreign customer remitted consideration in convertible currency (best-practice FATF-aligned evidence; not a standalone Swiss VAT statutory requirement)
Apple IAP/Google Play seller sales reports, customer geo-data and app store annual statements substantiating the digital service place-of-supply as foreign
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Swiss VAT audits (ESTV and cantonal tax authorities) may invalidate zero-rating and retrospectively claw back 8.1%/2.6%/3.7% VAT (depending on rate applicable at invoicing time) plus default interest (Art. 87 VAT Act, 4.5% p.a. minimum) if export documentation is incomplete, goods are demonstrably re-imported without justification, or the consideration is not paid within the standard commercial period (in practice, 180 days is the internal FTA reference for audit scrutiny — no formal statutory deadline exists; after 180 days, FTA may demand a written justification and, if unpaid, must re-verify the export condition). Penalties: negligent tax shortfall triggers a fine under Art. 102(1) VAT Act of up to 3% of the additional tax; deliberate tax evasion (artful measures to mislead, false export certificates) triggers a fine up to 3x the tax evaded (Art. 98(1) VAT Act); fraud, forgery or falsification of export proof is criminalized under Art. 117 VAT Act and Art. 251 Swiss Criminal Code (forgery of a document — 8.1% VAT clawback plus criminal imprisonment up to 5 years). The VAT reassessment period is 10 years for undeclared/recovered amounts in case of incomplete records (Art. 75 VAT Act — five years under regular returns, extended to ten years where no return was filed or tax evasion is determined).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) - Schweizerische Nationalbank (German), Banque Nationale Suisse (French), Banca Nazionale Svizzera (Italian).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland operates a fully liberalised capital and current account regime under the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments (CPIA) and the Foreign Exchange Ordinance (FEO). The Swiss franc is fully convertible; there are no exchange controls, approval requirements, or surrender obligations for current or capital account transactions. Dividend and profit remittances to foreign shareholders are unrestricted, subject only to Swiss corporate withholding tax of 35% (reduced or refundable under applicable double taxation treaties) and FATCA/CRS reporting obligations. A Swiss AG may open foreign-currency accounts abroad, receive inbound equity capital, and repatriate liquidation proceeds without central bank consent. The only practical hurdles are bank-level source-of-funds verification and, where relevant, sanctions screening under Swiss and international sanctions law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Swiss law imposes no statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds. App-store revenues earned from foreign jurisdictions may be retained in any currency and converted freely through any Swiss bank. The SNB requires banks to report cross-border flows for balance-of-payments statistics, but this does not create any surrender, retention, or conversion obligation for the exporting company.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) and Multi-Currency Operational Account (CHF/EUR/USD/GBP)
Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) and Operational Account in CHF with foreign-currency sub-accounts
Operational Account (Firmenkonto) in CHF and EUR

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low as primary treasury; Medium as auxiliary collection and payout channel. Legal constraints: Offshore electronic-money institutions (UK/EU EMIs such as Wise, Revolut Business, or Modulr) are not supervised as banks by FINMA and cannot provide a Swiss IBAN or hold Swiss settlement balances. A Swiss AG may use such EMIs for small-value multi-currency disbursements to foreign contractors, but FINMA Circular 2008/07 on outsourcing requires the Swiss relationship bank to know the complete payment chain, and treasury-critical liquidity must remain in a FINMA-licensed bank. Since the business model is an App Store freemium mobile utility, EMIs can be used only for non-core payouts; all capital injections, dividend flows, and reserve liquidity must be channelled through a Swiss regulated bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, tier-1 Swiss banks require physical presence of at least one authorised director or a duly mandated Swiss attorney for first-time corporate account opening. For capital escrow accounts, a compliance interview at a Swiss branch is nearly always mandatory. Remote submission of corporate documents is permitted, and some banks with fintech licences allow video-identification interviews for directors, but final account activation typically requires an in-person meeting in Switzerland or a meeting with a Swiss notary/consul abroad. The requirements derive from Article 3 of the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) and FINMA Circular 2016/07 on video and remote identification. A fully remote opening without any physical meeting is possible only with a narrow set of FINMA-regulated digital banks for low-risk, asset-light companies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctioned or high-risk jurisdiction exposure in the app user base or counterparty map, including availability in OFAC/FINMA-sanctioned territories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) technical geo-blocking configuration reports proving the app is unavailable in sanctioned territories; (ii) country/currency configuration screenshots from Apple App Store Connect and Google Play Console; (iii) sanctions-screening results for top corporate customers and vendors; (iv) a written export-control and restricted-party screening policy; and (v) contractual geoblocking clauses covering resellers, marketing affiliates, and payment processor restrictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership chain, such as a parent entity in a low-tax jurisdiction or nominee shareholder arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit (i) the full corporate ownership chain to ultimate natural persons; (ii) notarised and apostilled certificates of incorporation and shareholders' registers; (iii) beneficial-ownership declarations under Article 9 of the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance; (iv) an up-to-date Swiss commercial register extract for the AG; (v) a legal opinion from a Swiss licensed attorney confirming that the structure is transparent and does not involve bearer shares or nominee concealment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction patterns, including rapid pass-through movements, round-tripping, or outbound disbursements disproportionate to operating revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a treasury compliance file containing (i) the board-approved capital contribution resolution and notarial deed for any capital increase; (ii) contractual evidence for each outbound disbursement (cloud hosting agreements, App Store commission invoices, marketing contracts, software licence fees); (iii) app-store revenue statements from Apple and Google showing the legitimate business model; (iv) a cash-flow forecast explaining the timing of liquidity movements; and (v) a completed bank economic-purpose and transaction-fit questionnaire signed by the CEO/CFO.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital from a foreign shareholder must be routed as a SWIFT MT103 (ISO 20022 pacs.008) credit transfer to the Swiss AG's capital escrow account (Sperrkonto) at UBS AG or Zürcher Kantonalbank. The payment must identify the beneficiary by Swiss commercial register number (CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx) and include a clear purpose narrative in field 70 such as 'Kapitalerhöhung / paid-in share capital'; where the receiving bank requires a structured external purpose code, the relationship manager will map the transaction to the bank's equity-capital purpose category. Verification provisions: the bank requires (i) a certified copy of the notarial deed for the capital increase; (ii) the shareholders' or board resolution approving the contribution; (iii) proof of identity and source of wealth of the contributing shareholder; and (iv) confirmation that the funds are not derived from crime. After the capital increase is registered in the Swiss Commercial Register, the Sperrkonto is released for operational use upon presentation of the registration confirmation. No Swiss exchange-control approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operating disbursements for cloud Hosting, App Store commissions, marketing services, software licences, and remote contractors should be settled via FINMA-regulated Swiss payment rails: SIC/euroSIC for domestic transfers and SWIFT MT103 for cross-border foreign-currency payments. Each disbursement is backed by an underlying invoice, VAT statement where applicable, and sanctions-screening compatibility. For high-value service contracts, a letter of credit is uncommon; instead, use SWIFT MT103 against invoices or, where contractually required, a SWIFT MT700 confirmed letter of credit for physical-goods transactions. All payment messages should include the ISO purpose code assigned by the bank (such as 'SUPP' for supplier payments, 'LIC' for licence fees, or 'SOFT' for software royalties) and the company's Swiss UID.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX outrights in CHF/EUR/USD/GBP with no central bank approval
Outright FX forwards up to 24 months for committed commercial exposure
FX swaps for liquidity rolling and cross-currency cash-flow matching
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/CHF, USD/CHF) for asset-liability management
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for soft-currency app-store revenue where the foreign currency is not freely convertible in Switzerland
European-style OTC FX options under ISDA and CSA for risk management, subject to FINMA margin and market-abuse reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal, Cantonal and Municipal Corporate Income and Capital Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV); Canton Zug Tax Administration (Kanton Zug Steuerverwaltung)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year companies: filing due by 31 March following the fiscal year; extension commonly granted to 30 June upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 4.5% p.a. from the statutory due date; late-filing fines up to CHF 10,000; penalty for underdeclared tax up to 10% of arrears; persistent non-compliance triggers estimated assessment and enforcement proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quarterly Swiss Value Added Tax (VAT) Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly filing within 60 days after each calendar quarter; annual filing option for taxpayers with net VAT revenue below CHF 200,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 4.5% p.a. from the filing deadline; administrative fines up to CHF 8,000 for late filing; intentional VAT evasion fines up to CHF 30,000 plus late-payment interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Zug Compensation Fund (AHV-Vollzug) or registered compensation office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Employee copy due by 31 January following the wage year; electronic AHV declaration due by end of April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Employer liable for unpaid social contributions plus 4.5% interest; administrative fines up to CHF 30,000; managing directors and liquidators subject to joint and several liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Anticipatory Tax (Verrechnungssteuer) Declaration and Payment for Dividend Distributions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Declaration and payment within 30 days after any dividend or distribution; annual summary declaration may accompany the annual tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 4.5% p.a. for late payment; penalties up to the full tax liability for unreported distributions; violation exposes the Board of Directors to criminal prosecution under the Federal Anticipatory Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss Federal Statistical Office Annual Structural Business Survey
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (BFS); Canton Zug Office of Statistics
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Upon written request from BFS, typically due by 31 March for the preceding calendar year; mandatory for selected legal entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under the Swiss Statistics Ordinance for refusing to submit or knowingly submitting false data; no direct corporate tax consequence for timely compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit (Voltrevision) is mandatory for two consecutive years if two of three thresholds are exceeded: balance-sheet total CHF 20,000,000, annual revenue CHF 40,000,000, or 250 full-time employees; ordinary audit also mandatory for public or listed entities. Limited audit (Review) is required for companies not meeting ordinary audit thresholds but with more than 10 full-time employees; the shareholders may unanimously opt out of any audit if the company has fewer than 10 full-time employees (Art. 727a Swiss Code of Obligations).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957 onward); Swiss GAAP FER (facultative for SMEs); IFRS permitted for listed companies and accepted as equivalent under FINMA rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Switzerland does not maintain a public UBO registry and no annual external UBO confirmation is required for a private AG. The Board of Directors must keep the share register (Aktienbuch) continuously updated for every share transfer and report shareholding changes in the annual tax and capital tax return. Bearer shares, which historically required a mandatory beneficial-owner register, are effectively abolished for non-listed Swiss AGs; all new and converted shares are registered shares. Before each general meeting, the Board must certify the shareholder list for voting purposes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Executive Officers
Accounting Records, Business Correspondence and Supporting Documents (Art. 958d CO)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 650 - 1,300 per year for a registered office, domiciliation and administrative agent in Canton Zug
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,300 - 16,000 for a limited audit; USD 16,500 - 44,000 for an ordinary audit; USD 0 if audit opt-out applies and all shareholders unanimously consent

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% (federal corporate income tax levied on after-tax profit, equivalent to c. 7.83% pre-tax); combined federal + cantonal + communal headline for an ordinary Zug AG c. 14.6%; range across Swiss cantons c. 11.9%–21.0%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: STAF/OASI (2019/2020) incentives: patent/IP Box (90% exemption of qualifying IP income with a maximum 50% overall reduction of taxable profit), incremental R&D super-deduction (up to 50% of qualifying Swiss R&D labour costs, cantonal option), notional interest deduction on excess equity, and participation relief exempting 95% of qualifying dividend income and capital gains (≥10% holding held ≥1 year). A mobile utility app's software IP can qualify if the source code and development activity are economically anchored in Switzerland.
